name: Sahm Capital
legal_name: Sahm Capital Financial Company (a Single Person Joint Stock Company); formerly Valuable Capital Financial Company
founded: 2022 (established 20 Jan 2022 in Riyadh; CMA licence 22251-25 for dealing, custody and advising; operations began 1 Oct 2023; Sahm App launched Dec 2023)
ownership_summary: Wholly owned (100%, 9,375,000 shares, SAR 93.75m capital) by Valuable Capital Group Limited (VCGL) at 31 Dec 2025; the audited statements call VCGL the ultimate parent and controlling party. PIF-backed ewpartners (formerly eWTP Arabia Capital) led a USD 48m strategic investment in VCGL on 12 Feb 2025 (stake and valuation not disclosed); no investor sits directly in Sahm Capital.

shareholders.holder: ewpartners (PIF-backed; investor in the parent VCGL, not in Sahm Capital directly; USD 48m, stake undisclosed)

government_link: Indirect only: ewpartners, described as PIF-backed, led a USD 48m strategic investment in the parent group VCGL in Feb 2025 (S14). No state holding in Sahm Capital itself (S3).
group_structure: Sahm Capital Financial Company is the CMA-licensed Saudi operating entity of Valuable Capital Group Limited, which also has licensed entities in Hong Kong, the US, Singapore, the UAE and Kazakhstan (CEO speech, 5 Oct 2026). The UAE entity, Sahm Financial Limited (DIFC, DFSA ref F012218, company CL10742), is a VCGL subsidiary with the same chairman, not a subsidiary of Sahm Capital KSA. Brokerage technology, execution and clearing are bought from group affiliates (Valuable Capital Limited, Tickrs Clearing LLC), which charged SAR 126.9m and SAR 32.1m in 2025 (S3 note 13). Sahm Capital has a branch (CR 1010810235, named 'Sahm al-mal Professional Services Company' in the statements and 'Sahm Business Services Company' on the website) and opened a Jeddah customer-service office in 2026.

subsidiaries.name: Sahm al-mal Professional Services Company (branch, CR 1010810235)
subsidiaries.activity: Branch of Sahm Capital included in the financial statements; name differs on the website

footprint: Riyadh head office (KAFD) and a customer-service office in Jeddah (Al Zahra district, opened 2026). Services Saudi and US markets; onboards foreign individual investors worldwide from Feb 2026; UAE residents via Sahm Financial Limited (DIFC) from Sep 2026. Checked 2026-10-12.
customer_segments: Mass retail investors (no account or transaction minimums), active traders using margin and options, foreign individual investors onboarding to Saudi equities from Feb 2026, and UAE investors from Sep 2026.
business_lines: Digital stockbroking through the Sahm App: Saudi and US stocks, ETFs, options (US index options since Oct 2024), warrants, OTC, REITs, IPO subscriptions and margin (including Murabaha margin); Sahm AI assistant, Sahm Academy and Sahm Community. Brokerage commission and handling charges were 92% of FY2025 operating income. Licensed for fund management but asset management fee income was SAR 16,938 in 2025.

capabilities.wealth_summary: Sahm is a CMA-licensed digital brokerage (licence 22251-25: dealing, custody, advising, arranging, managing investments and operating funds) wholly owned by Valuable Capital Group, which sells and clears through affiliates. The Sahm App (launched Dec 2023) trades Saudi and US stocks, ETFs, options (US index options from Oct 2024), warrants, OTC, REITs, IPO subscriptions and margin (Murabaha margin certified Shariah-compliant by Raqaba), with a Sahm AI assistant, academy and community. It reports more than 2 million users (20 May 2026, undefined) and FY2025 operating income of SAR 494m with net income of SAR 79m, 92% from brokerage commissions and handling charges. No funds shelf, robo-advice, discretionary service, structured products or private markets were found, and asset management fee income was only SAR 16,938 in 2025. Sahm opened to foreign individual investors in Feb 2026 and to UAE investors through Sahm Financial Limited (DFSA licence Apr 2026, launch Sep 2026).

Execution and clearing services are bought from affiliates Valuable Capital Limited and Tickrs Clearing LLC (SAR 158.9m of charges in 2025).

opportunities: Shelf is trading only: no funds, robo, discretionary, structured or private-markets product found, despite licences to advise, manage investments and operate funds since Feb 2024 and a VP Advisory and Asset Management (S1, S2, S6).
Large retail base reported at 2m+ users (undefined) with foreign-investor onboarding from Feb 2026 and UAE access from Sep 2026, so a shelf could reach Saudi, foreign and UAE users (S12, S16, S11).
Profitable on SAR 494m of income in FY2025 and funding growth with heavy marketing (SAR 147.9m); low asset-management income (SAR 16,938) shows little recurring wealth revenue (S3).
Management frames a 'Learn, Analyse, Ask, Share, Invest' model and AI assistant (Sahm AI, over 1m interactions), pointing to appetite for AI-led engagement (S12, S13).
barriers: Technology, execution and clearing come from the parent group's affiliates (Valuable Capital Limited, Tickrs Clearing; VCGL says over 70% of staff are in R&D), and the Sahm chairman and vice chairman are respectively the Chief Strategy Officer and the CEO of the parent group (S2, S3, S10).
Product decisions are group-led and the Saudi management line is unclear: the management page names a different general manager from the one quoted until Feb 2025 (S2, S9, S24).
Mass-market, free-to-trade positioning (zero-commission offers, 0.105% Saudi fee) with no HNW or advisory proposition to attach a wealth shelf to (S4, S16).
Single-shareholder funding with a USD 6.15m Macao Development Bank loan due 1 Sep 2026 (S3).
incumbent_vendors: Valuable Capital Limited and Tickrs Clearing LLC - brokerage technology, execution and clearing from affiliates (S3)
Group in-house technology (Sahm App, Sahm AI) (S10, S12)

discrepancies.detail: Releases say more than 2 million users (20 May 2026) and 'registered users' (5 Oct 2026); the website shows registered users 1.5 million+, cumulative active users 3.3 million+ and cumulative downloads 3.8 million+. Earlier releases say over 1 million (Dec 2024) and 'nearly 70%' growth in 2025.
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded the 2m+ release figure and both website figures as indicative with definitions unresolved; no funded-account count exists.

discrepancies.detail: Official management page (read 2026-10-13) names Sze Yin Lee (Ryan) as General Manager and COO and no longer shows Hadeel Bedeeri, whose 'General Manager of Sahm Capital & Head of Dealing' biography is still in the site's text file but not displayed; company releases from Oct 2024 to Feb 2025 name Hadeel Bedeeri as General Manager; no 2026 release names either as GM.
discrepancies.resolution: Treated as a handover: Lee 'Verified current' on the official page; Bedeeri 'Requires verification' (no departure announcement, last named Feb 2025). Lee's start date and the date of the change are unknown; unresolved.

discrepancies.detail: The audited statements date it 2 Nov 2022 (8 Rabi II 1444H); the website says 19 Oct 2022; one search summary also said 19 Oct 2022.
discrepancies.resolution: Used the audited statements; the CMA register itself was not reachable.

discrepancies.detail: CMA announcement: licence approval 1 Feb 2024 (published 10 Oct 2024). Website: licensed 8 Feb 2024 and activities commenced 9 Oct 2024.
discrepancies.resolution: Used the CMA announcement (1 Feb 2024 approval).

discrepancies.detail: Website: 'Sahm Business Services Company'; financial statements: 'Sahm al-mal Professional Services Company' (CR 1010810235).
Statements list 'advisory, custody, dealing, fund operation and arranging'; the website lists dealing, custody, advising plus arranging, managing investments and operating funds.
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded the CMA announcement wording for the 2024 activities.

discrepancies.field: Andrew Chan: employer name and association post
discrepancies.detail: The website biography says President of Yuzhou Financial Holdings (Hong Kong) Limited and Vice Honorary Secretary of the Hong Kong Chinese Importers' and Exporters' Association; the 2025 board report says President of Sunhigh Financial Holdings Limited and Vice President of the association.
discrepancies.resolution: Kept the website wording in the title (official biography) and noted the board report wording; possibly a company rename, unresolved.

open_items: CMA public register not reachable (cma.gov.sa pages other than news announcements); licence 22251-25 and activities come from the company, its audited statements and CMA news items. DFSA public register returned HTTP 403, so the Sahm Financial Limited licence (ref F012218, CL10742) comes from company releases only.
No interim 2026 financials are published; H1 2026 and Q3 2026 results unavailable as at 12 Oct 2026.
Ownership above VCGL not researched (founders, ewpartners stake, other VCGL investors). 'Valuable Capital Group' headquarters and group accounts not found.

Execution and clearing set-up is inferred from related-party notes (Valuable Capital Limited, Tickrs Clearing LLC); the actual US clearing and custody chain and Saudi custody arrangements are not published.
The status of the USD 6.15m Macao Development Bank loan (due 1 Sep 2026) is unknown.
Jeddah office month (April 2026) and the December 2025 'nearly 70%' user growth release come from search results only.
Leads from internal notes: licence, ownership, users and international markets were confirmed; funding as a Sahm Capital round was not (the USD 48m was invested in the parent VCGL).

People pass 2026-10-13: the About page Management Team lists four people (Lee, Ejaz, Assaf, Saeed); neither a CEO nor a CFO is listed. Who the General Manager is stays the main open point: the page names Sze Yin Lee (Ryan), earlier releases (to Feb 2025) name Hadeel Bedeeri, and 2026 releases quote only the Chairman and the CFO. Check the CMA register (approved-person list) or ask the company before treating either as the day-to-day head.

The site's script file (S25) also holds biographies of two further independent directors, Yousef AlYousefi and Yi Song (Crystal), who are not shown in the board carousel and not in the 2025 board report's board of five; presumed former directors, not added and not verified.

2025 board report (S26): the fifth director is named in Arabic only ('Tshing Lee', non-executive); matching to 'Gary Lee' on the website rests on the seat and the board of five, not on a printed name. Non-executive Chairman and Vice Chairman and three further members; no executive director.

LinkedIn (role searches 2026-10-13, no names in queries): matches recorded for Huma Ejaz, Mahmood Saeed and Mohammed Asiri (S28-S30) and re-seen for the Chairman (S18); no profile returned for the General Manager, the former General Manager or the Vice Chairman (two profiles under his name at Valuable Capital entities show no title). Search results also show other Sahm staff not on the official page, for example a Head of Brokerage and Asset Management Operations; not added (no official listing).
Education fields left blank where the source gives no degree: Sze Yin Lee, Hadeel Bedeeri, Gary Lee. Career years are not published for any Sahm executive.
